clue.text: Church worker wanting a bob or two?

definitions.text: Church worker wanting a bob or two?

parts.words: Church worker wanting a bob or two?
parts.note: surface reading: someone employed by a church who is short of cash, a bob being an old shilling
setter's reading: a bob is a sequence in change ringing, so this person rings church bells

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the old British shilling, so 'a bob or two' reads as a little money; in bell-ringing, Plain Bob is a standard method of ringing the changes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person who studies or practises the ringing of bells, typically in a church tower.

clue.text: Novelist Roald's layers discussed by Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so what he says needs its first sounds exchanged

parts.note: Roald Dahl, the children's author
hens are egg layers
swap the opening sounds D and CH

explanation.surface: A spoonerist mangles something about the author Roald Dahl.
explanation.walkthrough: Dahl's chickens, with D and CH swapped, becomes Charles Dickens; 'layers' means egg-layers, not strata.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author of Oliver Twist and Great Expectations is one of the best-known writers of fiction.

clue.text: Mum next to lake by Taormina on vacation — a lovely island

parts.note: an informal word for mother
standard abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: vacating something empties it, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Sicilian resort

explanation.surface: Mum is holidaying by a lake near Taormina, in Sicily, and admires a nearby island.
explanation.walkthrough: Taormina is a real Sicilian town, and Sicily lies just north of the answer, so the holiday scene hangs together.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean country is an island nation south of Sicily, popular with tourists for its scenery.

clue.text: Where one might find a Constable just hanging around?

definitions.text: Where one might find a Constable just hanging around?

parts.words: Where one might find a Constable just hanging around?
parts.note: surface reading: where to find an idle police officer loitering
setter's reading: a painting by John Constable hung on a wall for display

explanation.walkthrough: The capital C gives it away: John Constable was an English landscape painter, and his pictures hang on walls rather than loiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings by famous landscape artists are displayed on the walls of public museums devoted to pictures.

clue.text: Old swan song in an alfresco setting

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old
a pen is a female swan
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An old swan song, a final performance, is given outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan song' looks like a fixed phrase meaning a farewell, but the words split: a female swan and a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means outdoors, and an event staged outside rather than under a roof takes place in the fresh atmosphere.

clue.text: Fresh taco baker unwrapped — popular snack item

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: removing a wrapper strips the outside, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A baker turns out fresh tacos, a popular snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The taco and baker suggest the Mexican snack, but only 'taco' is rearranged; the baker loses both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat biscuit made from oats, eaten with cheese, is a common savoury nibble in Scotland and Britain.

clue.text: Slowly move part of foot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to creep forward by small degrees
second meaning: one twelfth of a foot in imperial measure

explanation.surface: Someone with an injured foot can only shuffle along slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' suggests the body part, but it is the unit of length, which contains twelve of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for creeping forward gradually and a noun for a unit of length, a twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Highwayman fails to finish on time, exercising due depravity

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Dick Turpin, the notorious English highwayman, minus his last letter

indicators.note: exercise works and moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: standard abbreviation for time
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A highwayman who runs out of time shows a fitting wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman; in a down clue 'on' puts the time piece after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean moral corruption or wickedness; the answer is often found in the phrase moral turpitude.

clue.text: Failing MO makes dodgy laxative

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters cannot stay in their order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A failing modus operandi produces a suspect purgative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' looks like a link between wordplay and definition, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension of magnesium hydroxide in water, it is taken as an antacid and a mild purgative for constipation.

clue.text: Share veg grown here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a portion that is given out
second meaning: a small rented plot of land where people grow vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is also a small plot of council land rented out for growing vegetables, which is the sense the question mark points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a portion allocated to someone and also a rented garden plot for cultivating produce.

clue.text: A smallish dog, my Joe

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise
GI Joe is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone describes their friend Joe's little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but an exclamation, like 'cor!', a British cry of surprise; a GI is a US soldier, nicknamed GI Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh herding breed with short legs, famous as the Queen's favourite, is a small-to-medium pet.

clue.text: American shopping centre withdraws wool supplier

indicators.note: withdrawing is drawing back, so the letters run back the other way

parts.note: standard abbreviation for American
an American word for a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A US mall pulls out of a deal with its wool supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraws' reads as a business pulling out, but it turns the whole charade back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American animal is kept for its fleece, which is spun into yarn like sheep's.

clue.text: Open return trip taken by Indian VIP

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a raja is an Indian prince or king

explanation.surface: An Indian dignitary books an open return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open return' is a real kind of ticket, so the eye reads them together; in fact 'Open' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open, neither shut nor wide, is said to be in this state.

clue.text: Where to find Scottish believers in Starfleet commander?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Scots word for a church
second meaning: the captain of the starship Enterprise in Star Trek

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Star Trek captain has religious followers in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as 'among the fans of', but it only joins two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a church is where worshippers gather, and Captain James T. Kirk commands the Enterprise in Star Trek.

clue.text: Calling declaration

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vocation or occupation
second meaning: an open statement of belief

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like a verb, shouting out, which fits 'declaration'; it is the noun meaning a career.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a trade or vocation and also a public avowal, as in a profession of love or faith.

clue.text: Taps into new technology disciple

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

parts.note: solar power is a modern energy technology
the two taps on a basin are marked C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: A follower taps into the latest gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps into' looks like one verb meaning makes use of; split it, and the taps are the hot and cold ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a student or follower of a teacher, and a learned pupil can be called by this word.

clue.text: Irritated mega-whiny writer

indicators.note: someone irritated is put out and agitated, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An annoyed author has become extremely whiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins the fodder into one comic word; the answer is Ernest Hemingway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist, author of The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: RAF fume terribly, getting warmer

definitions.note: the answer is one of a pair of ear warmers

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly and out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The Royal Air Force is seething, getting hotter under the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' reads as a comparative adjective, hotter; it is a noun for something that keeps you warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover worn over the ear in cold weather keeps that part of the head from freezing.

clue.text: Swim Mersey, bracing dip!

indicators.note: to brace is to clasp or hold firm, so the phrase grips the letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An invitation to swim the Mersey, the river through Liverpool, for an invigorating plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bracing' fits a cold swim perfectly, which hides its job of holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip something is to plunge it briefly into liquid, which is to submerge it.

clue.text: Heading north, grocer gleefully embraces old master

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the phrase holds the letters inside

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A delighted grocer travelling north hugs a famous old painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters read upwards, as the down entry is written from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter before about 1800, and the Cretan-born artist of Toledo is one.

clue.text: Thin fabric put around oily cheese

indicators.note: putting something around turns it to face the other way

parts.note: fatty and oily are close in sense
the Greek sheep's cheese

explanation.surface: A thin cloth wrapped around a greasy cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put around' looks like a wrapping instruction for a container, but it turns only the oily piece back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a crisp, lustrous silk or rayon cloth used for evening gowns and linings.

clue.text: Free hot shakes from that

indicators.note: shaking tosses things about, so these letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Complimentary hot milkshakes, handed out from that stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakes' looks like a noun, milkshakes; it is the verb telling you to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal word means of that or arising from that thing, as in 'the cause thereof'.

clue.text: Agreeable family settled at last

parts.note: kin are relatives

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A pleasant family has finally put down roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled at last' reads as a family finally at home; it just keeps the end of 'settled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and kind both describe someone pleasant, friendly and considerate towards others.

clue.text: Regularly glimpsed long green monster

indicators.note: seeing something only at regular intervals catches every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A long green monster is often spotted, like a lake serpent sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Shrek, the famous green cartoon ogre, so the answer is in the picture too.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant from fairy tales who eats people is a classic example of a fearsome creature.

clue.text: Songwriter starts to sing in my own nightclub

indicators.note: a start is a beginning, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A songwriter sets out to perform at their own club.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Simon is the American songwriter of Simon and Garfunkel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Simon wrote hits such as Bridge over Troubled Water and The Sound of Silence.

clue.text: Steam a cauldron containing Chinese food here

definitions.note: a place: where Chinese food is eaten

indicators.note: a thing containing something holds it within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A recipe step: steam in a cauldron with Chinese food inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing Chinese food' reads as a cauldron's contents; 'containing' hides the answer, and 'here' makes the definition a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Portuguese colony on China's south coast is a region where Chinese cuisine is served.

clue.text: Murder victim left south of Lincoln

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A body was left south of the city of Lincoln, in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is also an English city, which suits a crime scene; in a down clue 'south of' puts the left piece underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son was killed by his brother Cain, the first killing in the Bible.

clue.text: Prince Andrew gutted when thrown in nick

indicators.note: something thrown in ends up inside the other thing

parts.note: to nick is to arrest or steal, as is to nab

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: Prince Andrew is devastated when sent to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, and 'nick' is British slang for prison; here they mean emptied and nab.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim prince or governor in Mughal India, a ruler of noble rank.

clue.text: Through which to view popular satirical magazine articles?

parts.note: Private Eye, the British satirical magazine
a written article is a piece

explanation.surface: A question about what to read to see how the satirists view things.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a long-running British satirical magazine, often just called the Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenses at the end of a telescope or microscope are what the observer looks through.

clue.text: Fish swimming around fountain well behind yard

indicators.note: one thing behind another comes after it, so the earlier-mentioned piece is placed second

parts.note: standard abbreviation for yard

indicators.note: swimming around means moving about in all directions, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A fish swims round a fountain behind a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' reads as an adverb, 'well behind', but it belongs to the fodder; 'behind' puts the rest after the yard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large ocean species of tuna with bright yellow fins, widely caught for food.
